column2: Send out four pulses. Up, up, up, down. Something bounces them back.
Slide a copy along what came back, and multiply the pulses that line up.
Pulses pointing the same way agree, and add a block. Opposite ways disagree, and take one away.
Lined up exactly, all four agree. A score of four, at the echo.
One step off, three pairs line up. Two agree, one disagrees. A score of one, where nothing is.
Slide all the way, and ghosts appear on both sides, a quarter the echo's size.
With more than one pulse, every pattern leaves ghosts. So send a second. Up, up, down, up.
Its ghosts are the same size, at the same shifts. What if we add the two rows?
Every ghost meets its opposite and cancels. Only the echo is left, twice as tall. Two bad echoes, and not a single ghost.
But the guarantee needs the same scene for both sends. Move the echo one step between them, and ghosts return.
Now two things echo back. A loud one, and a quiet one three steps farther.
Pattern A's two echoes overlap, and the receiver records their sum.
Score it as before. The loud one stands tall at zero. At three steps, where the quiet one is, the score is zero.
Zero is not empty. Each echo brings its own row of scores, and at three steps they collide.
The loud one's ghost there is minus four. The quiet one's peak is plus four. They cancel.
One step either side, the loud ghosts stand four tall, as tall as the quiet echo.
Pattern B's ghosts have the other sign. What will B score at three steps?
Eight. Its ghost lands on the quiet echo instead of erasing it, and doubles it.
Add the two rows. Thirty-two at zero, eight at three, zero everywhere else. The scene, eight times over.
Sending A twice would not help. Its ghosts never cancel themselves, so the quiet one stays hidden.
